Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Lands and Facilities, Director Intergovernmental Relations and Public Affairs, General Manager Parks, Recreation and Culture
Note from General Manager Lands and Facilities
:
The City recognizes and appreciates the notable service and valued dining experience that the current Hart House Restaurant operators have provided to Burnaby residents and visitors over many years.
The current lease for the Hart House Restaurant is approaching the end of its term. The City’s standard practice is to publicly advertise lease opportunities for City-owned facilities in order to ensure that public assets are used in the best way possible, for the benefit of Burnaby residents, and that the process is fair and transparent. The current operator, like any interested party, is welcome to participate in the process.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider publicly advertising Hart House Restaurant lease opportunity
agenda_briefs.summary: The City of Burnaby says the current lease for the Hart House Restaurant is nearing the end of its term. Following its standard practice, the City plans to publicly advertise the lease opportunity for this City-owned facility so the process is fair and transparent and the public asset is used in the best way possible. The current operator is welcome to take part in the process, just like any other interested party. No decision has been made yet on who will operate the restaurant next.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you want to run the Hart House Restaurant, watch for the City's public lease posting and prepare to submit a proposal.

agenda_briefs.title: Burnaby Council to consider Hall Avenue Loop / 7252 Kingsway corrective actions
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a report about the Hall Avenue Loop near 7252 Kingsway. A resident, Jean-Joseph Portelance, raised safety concerns, citing the unposted 50 km/h statutory speed limit under the BC Motor Vehicle Act, blind spots, and a disconnected pedestrian path. Staff from Lands and Facilities say they have contacted the writer and will work through any corrective actions. The resident requested temporary measures — repainting parking lines, adding Hall Avenue signage, speed bumps and a crosswalk — estimated at under $2,000. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on the Hall Avenue Loop report — it could affect access or traffic near 7252 Kingsway.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider paid parking expansion at Lake City and Production Way
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposal to expand paid parking around the Lake City Way and Production Way–University SkyTrain stations. The area currently sees high demand for long-term parking. If approved, staff would monitor parking demand and travel patterns after the change and assess whether future adjustments are needed. This is still a proposal — no decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — if you or your staff park near these SkyTrain stations, paid parking could soon apply.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Gilmore Place rezoning application in 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is expected to consider a rezoning application for the next phases of the Gilmore Place development in 2027. City staff say they are working with the applicant to move the application forward, and they will also follow up on a complaint about the construction site at the 4100 block of Dawson Street to make sure the property stays tidy and follows City bylaws while approvals are processed. No decision has been made yet, and the timing could change.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you own or operate a business near the Gilmore Place site, watch for the 2027 rezoning application and any public hearing dates.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Metro Vancouver report on growth infrastructure costs
agenda_briefs.summary: Metro Vancouver's study estimates about $115 billion in local, regional and provincial infrastructure investment is needed over the next 15 years to support 570,000 new homes identified in member jurisdictions' Housing Needs Reports. The MVRD Board received the report and forwarded it to member jurisdictions, TransLink, and provincial and federal ministers, directing staff to advance its recommendations and report back with options. The study is a high-level, order-of-magnitude estimate, not a detailed project forecast, and proposes a modernized infrastructure funding framework plus analysis of new revenue and financing tools.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for Burnaby Council's decision and any follow-up on new infrastructure funding tools that could affect development charges.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review RDOS climate action program correspondence
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to receive correspondence for information about the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen's letter to the Province supporting a minimum five-year renewal of the Local Government Climate Action Program (LGCAP) starting in 2027. The RDOS board passed its motion on September 3, 2026, and sent the letter September 10, 2026. This is an information item only — no vote, bylaw change, or new rule for Burnaby businesses is proposed. No action or compliance change is expected for local businesses.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider correspondence on 5416 and 5512 Buckingham Avenue
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider correspondence from Alicia Schuurmans and Nathan Brunner about the properties at 5416 and 5512 Buckingham Avenue. The item appears on the agenda as correspondence, and copies have been sent to the Chief Administrative Officer and the General Managers of Corporate Services and Planning and Development. No proposed bylaw, permit, or rule change is described in the agenda item, so it is not yet clear whether Council will take any action or simply receive the letter. If you own or operate a business near these addresses, this is an early signal that a development or property matter may be coming forward.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council decision on this item — a development or property change at these addresses could affect nearby businesses.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider living wage standards in Burnaby's Purpose Economy Strategy
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider adding living wage standards to the city's Purpose Economy Strategy, following a September 18, 2026 letter from resident Brian Hauk to the Social Planning Committee. Hauk asks that binding labour criteria — including a mandatory living wage, currently about $30/hr, plus fair working conditions — be built into the strategy before Council gives final approval, and that the city tie any endorsement or support of local businesses to enforceable labour standards. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council decision on living wage standards — it could affect your payroll costs and city contracts.

agenda_briefs.title: Burnaby Council to Consider Bike Lane Network Correspondence
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider correspondence from Svetlana Chen, supported by 35 additional names and addresses, calling for a cohesive bike lane network. The submission asks the City to follow TransLink's rapid implementation design guide to bridge gaps between disconnected protected bike lane segments, citing examples on Imperial St. near Marlborough Ave, Austin Rd. near North Road, and Willingdon Ave. near Beresford and Juneau Sts. No decision has been made yet. Because no privacy statement was included, the 35 supporting names and addresses were redacted from the public record.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the council agenda for any decision or staff referral on the proposed bike lane network, as road and parking changes could affect your business.
